subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-09-02 - a Nazi-looted Kandinsky heads to Christie's
html:
Nariway Signals
Tuesday, September 2, 2026
Orientation
Heaviest today on restitution turning straight into market event — a Kandinsky recovered from the Nazis after a six-year fight now heading to Christie's for eight figures — alongside a government pulling a commissioned painting off its own embassy wall for being ideologically inconvenient, a private Indigenous-art collection converting itself into public infrastructure north of the city, and a fresh museum directorship continuing weeks of leadership churn.
Lead
A Kandinsky restituted to Holocaust heirs is now Christie's October headline lot
Das bunte Leben (A Colorful Life) (1907) hung on loan at Munich's Lenbachhaus for more than five decades before Germany's Nazi-loot commission ruled in 2023 that it belonged to the heirs of German-Jewish collector Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermann — sold under duress in October 1940, months after the German invasion. It now leads Christie's Oct 14 London Evening Sale, estimated above $30M, which would place it among the three most expensive Kandinskys ever auctioned. It's the sharpest instance yet of a pattern this brief keeps tracking on the law-and-estates beat: a restitution ruling isn't the end of a collection's public life, it's often the opening bid of its next one.
Artnet · ARTnews
What's happening
A private Indigenous-art collection is converting itself into public space this fall
The Gochman Family Collection — founded 2021 by Becky Gochman and Zach Feuer, now 750+ works, mostly by Native artists, already loaned to 100+ exhibitions worldwide — opens a 10,000-sq-ft space in Katonah, NY this fall, under newly hired director Laura Phipps (16 years at the Whitney, where she co-chaired its Indigenous art working group). A clean, current instance of the same shape this brief tracks constantly: a living collector's holdings becoming standalone public infrastructure rather than a promised bequest.
The Art Newspaper · Hyperallergic
The State Department pulled a Kehinde Wiley off its own embassy wall
Young Artists After Siamesas 1960 was commissioned in 2013 with taxpayer funds for the Art in Embassies program — Wiley spent two years studying Dominican modernists and working with Santo Domingo art students to make it — and hung at the US Embassy there until officials called it "woke" and had it removed this month; a senior State Department official now says the agency is exploring the legality of deaccessioning it outright. A government-collection cousin of every donor-intent and deaccessioning fight this brief tracks on the private side, except here the "founder" whose intent is being overridden is the program itself.
The Art Newspaper
Cornell's Johnson Museum has its next director
Edouard Kopp, chief curator of Houston's Menil Drawing Institute (and before that Harvard Art Museums and the Getty), becomes the Johnson's Richard J. Schwartz Director on Nov 1, succeeding Jessica Levin Martinez, who left for the Corning Museum of Glass in February. Not a collector-founded institution, but the leadership bench this brief has tracked turning over for six straight weeks keeps resetting.
Cornell Chronicle
Worth reading
Roland-Philippe Kretzschmar, “Prestige Machines”
Reads Venice's 2026 edition — the first to skip awarding Golden and Silver Lions — as accidental proof of how manufactured "prestige" actually is: strip out the ranking machinery and what's left is which institutions still have the standing to anoint anyone at all. A useful frame for every founder-museum this brief tracks trying to buy or build that same standing from scratch.
The Art Bystander
Anne Parke, “Art for What's in Other Advisors' Inboxes”
A rare look inside what other advisors are actually recommending to clients right now — four advisories, three countries, thirteen artists — the kind of competitive transparency collecting advisors rarely offer each other in public.
Anne Parke Art Advisory

Christie's Hiroshige preview: 9 days out — inside two weeks
Public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 20 Rockefeller Plaza; already on Alina's calendar for the Sept 12 preview.
ARTnews
Bartos Mondrian tour opens its Zurich leg today; New York leg 15 days out
Public-view legs: Zurich Sept 2–4, Paris Sept 9–12, New York Sept 17–20, Hong Kong Sept 25–29, London from Oct 8, sale Oct 14 (£20–30M / $27–41M estimate).
ARTnews
Sotheby's Open House: 18 days out
Sept 20–21, Sotheby's NYC HQ. Its confirmed program includes a session on legal considerations across an art collection's lifecycle, staged by the house's own trusts-and-estates practice.
